title: Find the third angle of four triangles
description: The video takes the line through the top corner from the example in the book, which shows that the three angles make a straight angle. For each pair of angles it adds the two, takes the sum away from one hundred and eighty, and checks by adding all three.
teaching_notes: One idea: the third angle is what remains of one hundred and eighty degrees after the two given angles. Watch for students who take one of the given angles away instead of their sum.

source: Find the third angle of a triangle (using a parallel line) when two of the angles are: (a) 36°, 72° (b) 150°, 15° (c) 90°, 30° (d) 75°, 45°
video_script.why: The child has used a parallel line to show that the three angles of a triangle make a straight angle and now finds the third angle four times.
video_script.substitution: Add the two given angles, then take the sum away from one hundred and eighty degrees.
video_script.anchor: four pairs of angles: thirty six and seventy two, one hundred and fifty and fifteen, ninety and thirty, seventy five and forty five
video_script.payoff_line: The third angles are seventy two, fifteen, sixty and sixty degrees

final_answer.spoken: the third angles are seventy two, fifteen, sixty and sixty degrees

maths_rules: a line through the top corner parallel to the base makes the three angles of the triangle a straight angle, so they add to 180°
video_script.design: The four pairs stay in the anchor band. The working shows the sums, the take-aways from one hundred and eighty and a check by adding all three angles.

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>In the example in your book, a line through the top corner is parallel to the base.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The three angles of the triangle then sit side by side along that line.

beats.on_screen: To find: the third angle of each triangle

marks.find: the question is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the third angle of each triangle.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the alternate angles equal the two given angles, so the three angles make a straight angle: sum of the three angles = 180°

marks.alt: the two outer angles on the line are marked equal to the two given angles
marks.straight: the words sum of the three angles equals 180° are written

narration: <bookmark mark='alt'/>Step one, the two outer angles on the line are alternate angles. They are equal to the two given angles.
<bookmark mark='straight'/>The three angles make a straight angle, so they add to one hundred and eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, add the two given angles in each triangle. Thirty six plus seventy two is one hundred and eight.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One hundred and fifty plus fifteen is one hundred and sixty five.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Ninety plus thirty is one hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Seventy five plus forty five is also one hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, take each sum away from one hundred and eighty. For the first, one hundred and eighty take away one hundred and eight is seventy two.
<bookmark mark='b'/>For the second, one hundred and eighty take away one hundred and sixty five is fifteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check by adding all three angles: (a) 36° + 72° + 72° = 180°  (b) 150° + 15° + 15° = 180°

marks.a: the first check is written and a tick appears
marks.b: the second check is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step four, check the first two by adding all three angles. Thirty six plus seventy two plus seventy two is one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One hundred and fifty plus fifteen plus fifteen is also one hundred and eighty.

marks.cd: the last two take-aways are written

narration: <bookmark mark='cd'/>For the last two triangles, one hundred and eighty take away one hundred and twenty is sixty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The third angles are seventy two, fifteen, sixty and sixty degrees.
